THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Even though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties, it is taken up for hearing.

This appeal is filed under Section-173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 26.03.2014 passed in M.V.C. No.812/2011 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & Additional M.A.C.T., at Kundapura, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) for enhancement of compensation.

Brief facts:
3. The appellant was traveling in an Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-20B-6534 belonging to the 2nd respondent, driven by the 1st respondent and while the appellant was getting down at Matapady Nagaraj Poojary vs Rathnakar Nayak on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70388113/
2 Village, Udupi Taluk, suddenly the auto driver moved the vehicle in a very high speed and rash and negligent manner, as a result the appellant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

sentences.text: Immediately he was shifted to Mahesh Hospital, Brahmavara, thereafter to KMC Hospital, Manipal, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 15.05.2011 to NC: 2024:KHC:21252 20.06.2011, later he was shifted to Mahesh Hospital for further treatment.
4. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant under Section-166 of the M.V. Act, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the petition in part, and awarded a compensation of Rs.9,91,530/-
along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 and 3 therein, jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

5. Heard arguments of learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for respondent No.3/Insurance Company and perused the materials on record.
6.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded under various heads is on lesser side.
Therefore, seeks for enhancement of the compensation.

On the other hand, learned counsel appearing for the 3rd respondent - insurance company submits that the Tribunal is justified in passing the impugned judgment and award and there is no ground for enhancement.
That the compensation amount as awarded by the Tribunal is sufficient and adequate.

8. The Tribunal has awarded compensation under various heads as follows:
 Pain And Suffering : Rs. 70,000/-
 Medical Expenses : Rs. 1,43,330/-

Loss of earnings during laid : Rs. 55,000/-
 of period  Loss of future earning : Rs. 6,73,200/-
 capacity  Loss of amenities : Rs. 50,000/-

The appellant/claimant was 27 years old and has suffered injuries and disability in the road traffic accident i.e., while he was getting down from the autorickshaw, NC: 2024:KHC:21252 because of the rash and negligent driving by the driver of the autorickshaw, he fell down and as per Ex.P6 the wound certificate, he suffered the following injuries:-

3
1. Laceration 1 x 0.5 x 2 cms over right small finger on palmer aspect.

2. Abrasion over left elbow and forearm 10 x 7 x 0.2 compensation.
3.
Contusion
left shoulder

. 
4. Laceration of left eyebrow 3 x 1 x 1 compensation.
5.
Abrasion of left molar region.

6. Laceration of chin 2 x 1 x 0.5 cms.
10.
The Doctor PW.3 has given Psychological report- Ex.P11(a).

PW.3 on examination stated in the evidence that the claimant has suffered severe head injury resulting in loss of memory, vision,
speech and locomotive functions.
It is the opinion of the Doctor/PW3 that the claimant has suffered cognitive disability affecting his brain and is unable to work as he was doing prior to the accident.

In the year 2023 the claimant has received Unique Disability Certificate with I.D. Card from the NC:
2024:KHC:21252 Government of Karnataka that the claimant has suffered locomotor disability of 50%.
Therefore, the claimant has suffered significant disability affecting his career.
The claimant has become disabled person mentally and physically and not responding properly to the wordly affairs.
Accordingly his mother stood as a guardian to the claimant and filed claim petition.

Though PW.3 has not assessed the percentage of the disability, but from the evidence of Doctor PW.3 and other medical evidence, the injuries sustained by the claimant is very significant one affecting his brain capacity with locomotive functions.
But the Tribunal has only considered the permanent physical disability at 60%.
The Tribunal has committed error in assessing percentage of disability.
It is not disputed that the claimant was doing Electrician work, at this young age of 27 years, the claimant has suffered severe injuries to the head ruining his entire career.
Though the Doctor PW.3 has not stated in her report, what would be the functional disability suffered by the claimant.

But it is proved that the claimant's brain function is diminished NC: 2024:KHC:21252 impairing his speech,
vision and causing memory loss.
An Electrician job requires the movement of hands and legs including the fingers.
Due to the locomotor disability, the claimant cannot continue to work as an Electrician permanently, which results in loss of avocation.
Therefore, considering all these aspects and considering the principle of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAJ KUMAR Vs. AJAY KUMAR AND ANOTHER reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

entities.text: RAJ KUMAR Vs. AJAY KUMAR AND ANOTHER reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: it would be appropriate to take 90% as functional disability.
11. The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of future prospects in life and also has not awarded any compensation towards loss of marriage prospects.
The claimant was aged 27 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, certainly the claimant is entitled to compensation towards loss of future prospects in life.
As the disability affected is a significant one and permanent in nature.
Therefore, the functional disability is taken into consideration as 90%.

Therefore,
considering the NC: 2024:KHC:21252 judgment of Division Bench of this Court in NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY VS. ABDUL S/O MEHABOOB TAHASILDAR and Hon'ble Apex Court in SIDRAM VS. sentences.text: 4 ANOTHER therefore, 40% of the income is added towards loss of future prospects in life.
The accident occurred on 18.05.2011, therefore the notional income is taken at Rs.6,500/- per month.
The appropriate multiplier is '17' x 40%.

Hence the loss of future prospects in life would come to :-
Rs.6,500 + 2600 (40% of Rs.6,500) x 17 x 12 x 90/100 = Rs.16,70,760/-
12.
The medical expenses of Rs.1,43,330/- is kept intact and there is no changes since the claimant was inpatient for 99 days in the Hospital.
Therefore, the compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering.
Rs.75,000/- is awarded towards laid up period.
Towards Food and nourishment a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded.
Towards future medical - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:21252 expenses a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded.
Towards loss of amenities in life a sum of Rs.75,000/- is awarded.
Towards Loss of marriage prospects a sum of Rs.75,000/- is awarded.

13. Hence, the appellant is entitled for a total enhanced compensation under various heads as follows:
a. Pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
b. Medical Expenses Rs.1,43,330/-
c. Loss of future prospects Rs.16,70,760/-
 d. Laid up period Rs. 75,000/-
 e. Loss of amenities Rs. 75,000/-
 f. Future medical expenses Rs. 50,000/-
 g. Food, Nourishment,
 Conveyance Rs. 50,000/-
 h. Loss of marriage prospects Rs. 75,000/-
 ______________  TOTAL Rs.22,39,090/-
 ______________ 14.
Therefore, the appellant is awarded a total compensation of Rs.22,39,090/- as against the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.9,91,530/-.

5 NC: 2024:KHC:21252

Hence, the appellant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.12,47,560/- (Rs.22,39,090 - Rs.9,91,530), along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

15. Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 26.03.2014, passed in MVC No.812/2011, on the file of Senior Civil Judge and Additional Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal, Kundapura, is modified to an extent that the appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.12,47,560/- (Rupees Twelve Lakhs Forty Seven Thousand Five Hundred and Sixty Only), along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till realization in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
